correctness.rationale: Poisson u_a(k) is log-concave with interval support; the kernel u_a(x−z) is TP2. Product of all latent factors is MTP2, and marginalization over common Z preserves it (Fallat et al., Prop3.4(ii)). The joint pair-sum coefficient kernel g(x,s)=[t^(s−x)]e^(at)(a+bt)^x/x! has adjacent minors equal to nonnegative log-concavity expressions, establishing LR monotonicity for every pair. Since S_n=T_n+nZ, T_n~Pois(na), condition on S_n=n−1 gives Bin(n−1,1/n), and on S_n=n gives w Bin(n,1/n)+(1−w)δ1 with w=(na)^n/n! divided by that plus b. Therefore the tail-2 gap changes sign exactly at b_ST=(na)^n/n! * δ_n/r_n with r_n=Pr(Bin(n−1,1/n)≥2) and δ_n=(n−1)/n²(1−1/n)^(n−2). At n=3, exact conditional mass ratios yield LR iff b≤2a³, ST iff b≤6a³. Independently checked exact rational thresholds at n=3..12 for b/bcrit=1/2,1,2; finite samples corroborate but universal proof is analytic.

value.rationale: A sharp structural boundary of dependent conditional ordering in a canonical MTP2 positively correlated multivariate Poisson model. Exact distinct LR/ST cutoffs provide reusable risk/association counterexamples with explicit dimension dependence, beyond mere numerical nonmonotonicity.

final_claim: For equi-intensity common-shock counts Xi=Yi+Z, Yi independent Pois(a), Z Pois(b), a,b>0, the joint law is MTP2 and pair-sum conditional distributions are LR-increasing. For every n≥3 the full-total tail event {X1≥2} at totals n−1,n reverses exactly when b>b_ST(n,a); at n=3 the LR and ST frontiers for totals 2,3 are b=2a³ and 6a³.
limitations: Sharp frontiers are only the declared adjacent pair/tail; no global full-total order phase diagram.
Possible equivalent examples in older actuarial/total-positivity literature remain a bounded residual risk.
